title: Rust vs C: the same memory bug, caught at different times
audience: Programmers curious about Rust's memory safety

slides.title: It compiles
slides.speaker_notes: This C program frees memory, then reads it anyway. It compiles, runs, and prints garbage.
slides.visual_beat: C code types in; free(p) line highlights; terminal shows the build succeeding and the garbage number.

slides.title: Use after free
slides.speaker_notes: The pointer still holds the old address. The heap block was handed back, but nothing stops you from following the arrow. That's a use after free. G-C-C can warn about it, but it still builds.
slides.visual_beat: Pointer box p arrows into a heap block holding 42; block turns dashed (freed); arrow still followed; value becomes garbage; gcc -Wall warning line appears, then 'build ok'.

slides.title: Rust says no
slides.speaker_notes: Now the same bug in Rust. The reference borrows the data, then you drop the owner while the borrow is still in use. The compiler refuses to build it: cannot move out of data, because it is borrowed.
slides.visual_beat: Rust code; data owner box and view borrow arrow; drop(data) line highlights red; rustc error E0505 appears.

slides.title: Before it exists
slides.speaker_notes: Same mistake. C lets it reach runtime. Rust stops it before the code ever runs.
slides.visual_beat: Two columns: C -> runtime (red), Rust -> compile time (accent). Payoff frame.
